catalog_quote: Stress is a non-segmental feature expressed by heightened pitch, length and loudness in the stressed syllable. Stress in WC Bajau normally occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word. Because of its predictable nature, stress in WC Bajau is non-phonemic. ... The penultimate stress rule applies to the phonological word, which is not necessarily the lexical word. ... 2.3.1.2.1 Regular ultimate stress with penultimate schwa WC Bajau is the only Sama-Bajaw language which does not have universal penultimate stress (Pallesen (1979:127), owing to the fact that the schwa vowel /ə/ in WC Bajau generally does not bear stress. ... Hence, stress has “reverted” to the ultimate syllable in WC Bajau words where /ə/ is the vowel in the penultimate syllable. ... 2.3.1.2.2 Irregular stress The exceptional stress pattern observed with the schwa vowel is regular. sources.quote: 'Primary stress in PSB occurs regularly on the vowel of the penultimate syllable of the word ... in all SB languages except in predictable environments in NB. ... In NB [North Borneo/Sabah Land Bajaw = West Coast Bajau, NB.1 Kota Belud] stress occurs on the penult except when the vowel of the penult is the mid central vowel /ə/, in which case it occurs on the ultima. This stress shift is accompanied by the reduction to a single consonant of an inherited geminate; e.g. PSB *bəlli "to buy" (NB.1).'
